source_title: Kedarnath witnesses fresh snowfall; videos go viral as netizens call the views a 'heavenly sight' - The Times of India
source_excerpt: Kedarnath Dham looks straight out of a postcard right now! Fresh snowfall has covered the famous Shiva shrine and the surrounding Himalayan peaks in white, and pictures and videos of the beautiful scene are quickly finding their way across social media.Located in Uttarakhand's Rudraprayag district, Kedarnath received fresh snowfall on October 29, giving devotees and visitors a glimpse of the mountains in their winter colours. And while the sight has left many people online admiring its beauty, the sudden change in weather has also brought a noticeable chill to the region.According to reports, this was Kedarnath's second spell of snowfall within a week. The India Meteorological Department recorded around 0.4 cm of snow between Wednesday evening and Thursday morning. The snowfall also affected other high-altitude areas, including Gangotri.Kedarnath's snow-covered temple leaves netizens mesmerisedAs soon as visuals of the snowfall started circulating online, people couldn't stop talking about the views.The temple, surrounded by snow-covered mountain slopes, looked particularly beautiful in the videos shared on social media. One such video was posted by the X account @ILoveSiliguri, showing fresh snow falling at Kedarnath Dham.One user shared the video with a heartfelt caption, writing:"Fresh snowfall at the sacred Kedarnath Dham in Uttarakhand. The snow-covered Himalayan peaks and the divine aura of Baba Kedar create a truly mesmerizing spectacle. A heavenly sight where the beauty of nature meets the divine presence of Mahadev."Another user described the fresh snowfall as a "breathtaking spectacle".For devotees of Lord Shiva, the visuals have made the occasion even more special. The combination of the ancient temple, white mountain peaks and falling snow has given the shrine a completely different appearance.Snowfall doesn't stop devotees from visiting KedarnathDespite the cold, devotees haven't stopped arriving at the temple to offer prayers.Videos circulating online show pilgrims standing outside the shrine in raincoats and carrying umbrellas as snowfall continues around them. Some can also be seen capturing the unusual weather on their phones.The scene has caught people's attention for another reason. Even with temperatures dropping, devotees are making the journey to seek Baba Kedar's blessings before the temple closes for the winter.However, authorities have asked visitors not to take the changing weather lightly.The district administration has advised pilgrims to wear proper winter clothing and follow the safety instructions issued by the administration and police. Visitors have also been asked to carry essential medicines and check weather conditions before travelling.IMD predicts more rain and snowfall in UttarakhandThe snowfall at Kedarnath comes amid a spell of unsettled weather across Uttarakhand.Dr CS Tomar, Director of the Meteorological Centre in Dehradun, said on October 30 that rainfall activity was expected to continue across parts of the state. The hill districts, in particular, could experience more light to moderate showers, while higher-altitude areas may receive further snowfall.The weather department has indicated that precipitation could continue at isolated places over the northern hill districts on October 31, November 1 and November 2, although the activity is expected to gradually ease.The India Meteorological Department's latest Char Dham weather update for October 30 also listed the possibility of light rain along the Rudraprayag-Kedarnath route.Authorities are keeping an eye on weather conditions and have urged pilgrims to stay updated before setting out for the shrine.When will Kedarnath temple close for 2026?For those planning a visit, there's another important date approaching.The Kedarnath Temple is scheduled to close its doors for the winter season on November 11, 2026, at 8:30 am. After the closure, the ceremonial procession carrying the deity will begin its journey towards the winter seat at Omkareshwar Temple in Ukhimath, where worship will continue during the colder months.Until then, devotees are continuing to visit the shrine, even as the weather becomes increasingly cold.The fresh snowfall has certainly made Kedarnath look spectacular. But beyond the beautiful pictures and social media reactions, visitors heading towards the temple should remember that Himalayan weather can change quickly. Carrying warm clothes, checking official updates and following local instructions are essential.For now, the snow-covered Kedarnath visuals have given netizens a sight they'll want to keep looking at.
